events.instrument: Ley N° 21.590, modifica la ley N° 21.325 para ampliar el plazo de privación de libertad para la materialización de las expulsiones administrativas
events.what_changed: Raised the maximum detention to carry out an expulsion from 48 hours to five calendar days. It did not touch the list of detainee rights in inciso 2, including N° 4 (the right to communicate with one's consular representative), so it does not affect this indicator.
events.passage: Artículo único.- Sustitúyese en el inciso final del artículo 134 de la ley N° 21.325, de Migración y Extranjería, la expresión "cuarenta y ocho horas" por la frase "cinco días corridos".

answers.implementation_then_now: The law is the same on both dates. Art. 134 N° 4 has read 'Comunicarse con su representante consular' since the original text of 12 February 2022 and in every later version. On practice: in May 2025 the national torture-prevention mechanism (CPT) reported on its visits to police facilities holding migrants for administrative expulsion between November 2023 and October 2024. According to the press summary, it found 'la falta de garantías procesales básicas' in administrative detention. That suggests the art. 134 safeguards are applied unevenly, but the summary does not single out consular contact. I found no source documenting consular access specifically for either period. The MRD's starting rating, 'Effectively Always; Rarely', is not an allowed option (the two levels are not neighbours), so I mapped it to the midpoint, 'Sometimes; Usually', for both dates. I found no documented shift.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The MRD's implementation rating 'Effectively Always; Rarely' is not an allowed value, since the two levels are not neighbours. It probably rates two contexts separately. I recorded it as 'Sometimes; Usually'. On the law, the 'Yes' holds, but it is narrow. Art. 134 N° 4 covers only people detained to carry out an expulsion. A separate provision on reconducción in Title VI requires that a person being reconducted be guaranteed the chance to 'Contactar a familiares, a cualquier otra persona cercana o al cónsul de su respectivo país'. The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, which Chile has ratified, was not separately checked.
answers.notes: The answer rests on the statute only (Ley 21.325, art. 134 inciso 2 N° 4, read in the consolidated text). No court ruling was relied on. Ley 21.655 (in force 20-02-2024) amended art. 131 inciso 2 (wider scope for reconducción). It did not amend the consular-contact guarantee for reconducted persons or art. 134.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.article: Art. 134 inciso 1 ('En ningún caso se aplicará esta medida a niños, niñas o adolescentes')
Art. 4 inciso 2 (children not subject to migration sanctions)

events.what_changed: Raised the maximum detention for executing an expulsion from 48 hours to five calendar days. The bar on detaining children in inciso 1 was left untouched, so the indicator is not affected.
events.passage: Artículo único.- Sustitúyese en el inciso final del artículo 134 de la ley N° 21.325, de Migración y Extranjería, la expresión "cuarenta y ocho horas" por la frase "cinco días corridos".

events.instrument: Ley N° 21.655, modifica la Ley N° 20.430 ... y la Ley N° 21.325, en relación con la medida de reconducción
events.what_changed: Extended immediate reconducción to people who have already entered irregularly up to 10 km from the land border or within territorial waters, and raised the provisional entry ban from six months to one year. It does not touch the bar on detaining children in art. 134. It does widen the border procedure in which de facto holding of children has been reported.
events.passage: Artículo 2º.- Modifícase el inciso segundo del artículo 131 de la ley Nº 21.325 ... b) Reemplázase la frase "ya sea por pasos habilitados o no, o valiéndose de documentos falsificados", por la siguiente: "ya sea por pasos habilitados o no, o que se haya internado al territorio nacional hasta 10 kilómetros del límite fronterizo terrestre ..." ... d) Reemplázase la expresión "seis meses" por "un año".

answers.implementation_then_now: The law is the same on both dates. Since the original text of 12 February 2022, art. 134 has said that detention to carry out an expulsion 'En ningún caso se aplicará ... a niños, niñas o adolescentes'. On practice: the national torture-prevention mechanism's annual report covers August 2023 to December 2024 and was presented to the Chamber of Deputies in October 2025. It visited border 'containment' sites in the north and said that, although these are not designed as places of detention, 'en la práctica funcionan como tales'. It raised concern for both unaccompanied and accompanied children. That points to de facto holding of children at the border, while I found no report of children held in expulsion detention under art. 134. The evidence is thin and roughly the same across the window, so 'Usually' is kept for both dates and no shift is recorded.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' is defensible but narrow. Art. 134 bars only detention to carry out an expulsion, and art. 4 exempts children from migration sanctions. Neither expressly covers holding children during reconducción at the border, where the CPT reports de facto detention.
answers.notes: The answer rests on the statute only (Ley 21.325, art. 134 inciso 1, read in the consolidated text). No court ruling was relied on.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been no right protections neither in 2023 nor in 2026

events.instrument: Ley N° 21.590, modifica la ley N° 21.325 para ampliar el plazo de privación de libertad para la materialización de las expulsiones administrativas
events.what_changed: The maximum detention to carry out an expulsion went from 48 hours to five calendar days. Detention on the basis of migration status (to enforce expulsion) was already allowed and is now allowed for longer, so the answer stays 'No'.
events.passage: Artículo único.- Sustitúyese en el inciso final del artículo 134 de la ley N° 21.325, de Migración y Extranjería, la expresión "cuarenta y ocho horas" por la frase "cinco días corridos".

events.what_changed: Widened immediate reconducción to irregular entrants found within 10 km of the land border or in territorial waters, and to people who have already entered. This widens border removal; it creates no prohibition on detention.
events.passage: a) Reemplázase la expresión "intentando ingresar" por "intentando ingresar o habiendo ingresado". b) ... "o que se haya internado al territorio nacional hasta 10 kilómetros del límite fronterizo terrestre o dentro del mar territorial ..."

answers.implementation_then_now: Does not apply: there is no prohibition on detention based on migration status on either date. On practice, the CPT documented deprivation of liberty of migrants awaiting administrative expulsion in police facilities between November 2023 and October 2024, and border containment sites working in practice as places of detention. This confirms that migration detention is used, and it was extended in law in August 2023.
